name: Cave Vinicole de Hunawihr Gewurztraminer Rosacker 2017
text:
## Cave Vinicole de Hunawihr Gewurztraminer Grand Cru Rosacker 2017

**The story.** The Cave Vinicole de Hunawihr is the growers' cooperative of [Hunawihr](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Cave+Vinicole+de+Hunawihr,+Hunawihr,+France&t=k), a village on the Alsace wine route about 12 km north-west of [Colmar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colmar), and one of the "most beautiful villages of France" ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hunawihr); [Opimian](https://opimian.ca/cave-vinicole-de-hunawihr/)). Vines are recorded in Hunawihr as far back as 1123. At the end of the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II) the Alsace vineyard was devastated and neglected, and small growers struggled to recover alone; in 1954 Hunawihr's growers decided to join forces, making and selling their wines together. The online merchant vino.com describes it as the first cooperative in Alsace and the third in France ([vino.com](https://www.vino.com/fr/produttore/hunawihr), in French; the Guide Hachette also dates it to 1954 ([Guide Hachette](https://www.hachette-vins.com/guide-vins/les-vins/cave-vinicole-de-hunawihr-rosacker-tokay-pinot-gris-2002-2005/20055592))).

Today the co-op has about 130 members and makes some 2 million bottles a year ([Opimian](https://opimian.ca/cave-vinicole-de-hunawihr/)). It farms around 200 hectares around Hunawihr, [Riquewihr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riquewihr), [Ribeauvillé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ribeauvill%C3%A9) and Zellenberg, 13 of them in the grands crus Rosacker, Froehn, Sporen, Schoenenbourg and Osterberg. Each vineyard and parcel is pressed gently and fermented separately in stainless steel ([vino.com](https://www.vino.com/fr/produttore/hunawihr)). Its range climbs from the fresh, fruity "Réserve" wines, through the single-site lieux-dits and Vieilles Vignes, to the grands crus and the sweet Vendanges Tardives and Sélections de Grains Nobles ([vino.com](https://www.vino.com/fr/produttore/hunawihr)).

**How these bottles reached Canada.** Hunawihr's wines come to Canada through [Opimian](https://opimian.ca/), the non-profit, member-owned wine club founded in 1973, which offers them in its "Cellar" releases; its tasters' notes are quoted below ([Opimian](https://opimian.ca/cave-vinicole-de-hunawihr/)).

**The grape: Gewurztraminer.** [Gewürztraminer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gew%C3%BCrztraminer) means "spice Traminer" or "perfumed Traminer": a pink-skinned, extra-aromatic mutation of the ancient Traminer grape, named after the village of Tramin in South Tyrol. Its signature is lychee, and in fact Gewürztraminer and lychees share the same aroma compounds; it often adds roses and spice, and usually finishes off-dry. The longer name was first used in Alsace in the 1870s ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gew%C3%BCrztraminer)).

**The vineyard: Rosacker.** Rosacker is a [grand cru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alsace_Grand_Cru_AOC) and the co-op's flagship, on the south-east-facing slope of the village itself; its limestone-rich soils are said to give a very mineral expression ([Opimian](https://opimian.ca/pinot-gris-grand-cru-rosacker-aoc-alsace-13070/)). The Guide Hachette calls it Hunawihr's most famous terroir ([Guide Hachette](https://www.hachette-vins.com/guide-vins/les-vins/cave-vinicole-de-hunawihr-rosacker-tokay-pinot-gris-2002-2005/20055592), in French).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [Alsace vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/alsace) rates 2017 a very good vintage, with excellence across all varieties and sweetness levels; the one drawback was yields cut by up to a third, mostly by spring frost.

**What the critics say for 2017.**
- **Opimian's tasting note** ([Opimian](https://opimian.ca/lieu-dit-grand-cru-case-cave-vinicole-de-hunawihr-10421/)): deep yellow, with intense honeydew melon, honey, fresh fruit and lemongrass and a savoury edge; supple, with lemon and grapefruit. "A really classy wine with complexity, elegance and depth and a style which is unique to Alsace." Opimian adds that 2017's devastating spring frosts cut yields dramatically, especially for Gewurztraminer, and the hot summer that followed gave concentrated wines.
- I couldn't find a critic's score for this wine.
- Your CellarTracker list has no community score for this wine.

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is nine years old, and your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2020 to 2023. Grand cru Gewurztraminer from a concentrated year can outlast such a cautious window, but this is now the one to open first among your Hunawihr bottles. Expect honey, candied citrus and spice. Serve at 10 to 12°C.

**Food.** In Alsace, Gewurztraminer goes with Munster cheese, spicy Asian food and fruit tarts. With this one: foie gras, or a washed-rind cheese such as Munster.

**Value and where to buy.** None of the stores on this site lists Hunawihr's wines; in Canada they are sold through Opimian's member offers. For another Rosacker, BSW Liquor has Eblin-Fuchs's Grand Cru Rosacker Riesling 2016 at $65.99.

**Curious details**
- **Kings and emperors in the vineyards.** Alsace's best sites were singled out early: in 613 the future king Dagobert gave vines on the Steinklotz to an abbey, and in 777 Charlemagne's envoys reported favourably on the wines of the Marckrain at Bennwihr. The Alsace Grand Cru appellation itself only came in 1975, and there are now 51 grands crus ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alsace_Grand_Cru_AOC)).
- **Why "Tokay"?** Pinot Gris is said to have been brought back to Alsace from Hungary by General [Lazarus von Schwendi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lazarus_von_Schwendi) after his 16th-century campaign against the Turks, and planted under the name "Tokay". The name was phased out under an agreement with Hungary and dropped altogether in 2007 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alsace_wine)).
- **France and Germany, back and forth.** Alsace has changed nationality several times, which is why it is the only French appellation to label mostly by grape variety, as the Germans do ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alsace_wine)).
